title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: Thou with thy wife and other Friend, from in your parts are often brought very fresh into my remembrance with near affection, and many time have I taken my pen to write. And sometimes after writing have been discouraged sending, by its being so little worth and perhaps out of Season, before an opportunity of conveyance. But as iron sharepeneth iron, so doth the countenance of a man, his friend (as said the wise man). Even so I have thought it has that effect when we can convey a few lines from one to another where we have not the opportunity of the outward countenance.

Dear Friends, I feel a freedom in love to inform that the acceptable visit paid to us by our endeared Jersey Friends retains a good savor in the minds of Friends, and believe it had a quickening tendency, though there don’t appear that improvement that is desired. We have likewise had several religious visits of late. Jonathan Write from Virginia, Ruth Hagget & Rachel Dicks from Carolina who attended the Quarterly meeting.

There has been a large number of Friends moved out from North Carolina who have produced certificates from the Monthly meetings, as also a particular account front the Quarterly meeting there of the proceedings of friends and suppose two Monthly meetings are dissolved by the movement. Some few Friends that are left are joined to other Monthly meetings. They are about to purchase a body of land and as soon as convenient, to settle it.
O, may it not be truly said the harvest is great and the skillful faithful laborers few in comparison. Oh, that the number of faithful may increase everywhere, that truth may grow & prosper.

At this time John Hall from Europe and Stephen Grellet, his companion, are on a Religious visit to the meetings this side of the mountains. John Haines’ son at Crooked Run has accompanied them. Stephen appeared to have a clear discerning of the poor state we were in as to the life of religion.

We are in a good degree favored with health, as well as partakers of other Blessings which are bountifully bestowed upon us poor unworthy creatures. & that we may be thankful receivers is what I ardently desire.

I feel a desire that we may be preserved from the many snares of the grand adversary. But oh, my frailties and many besetments are at times heavy upon me, that I desire the prayers of those that are admitted in to favor, that they may intercede for me & mine, lest we become stumbling blocks and and castaways.

the 8th month 15th 1800— May add that opportunities have been missed of sending my lines, & now there appears another. Inform that we are in a tolerable state of health at present, though several of us have been poorly of late. There has been a very hot spell of weather–we have had an extraordinary harvest of grass & grain. There appears likely to be a dry spell at present. May we not say in truth what shall we render unto the Lord for all his blessings, for they are manyfold.

The love I at times feel for my Friends is not easily to be expressed. Please to remember my love affectionately to Dear Elizabeth and Rebecca, with others as opportunity offers and accept of the same.

postscript.p: (for John and Ruth Collins) excuse my poor writing & not expose it
